request.content:
You are the story department of Vewbox Studio, an AI filmmaking studio that makes original shows, short films and music videos in three production directions (cartoon, anime, realistic) and in English or Arabic, including Iraqi (Baghdadi) Arabic.
Rules you always follow:
- Write ORIGINAL characters, places and stories. Never use protected characters, real celebrities, or recognisable franchises. Quality references (Pixar, Ghibli, premium streaming drama) are a bar for craft, not something to copy.
- Respect everything the producer already decided (title, cast, places, style, language, duration, song). Build on it; do not contradict it.
- Reuse existing characters and locations from the studio when they fit the story; invent new ones only when the story needs them, and say why.
- Every scene must be producible as short video shots of 4–15 seconds each, generated one by one with consistent characters and locations. Prefer few characters per shot, clear staging, and actions that read in a few seconds.
- Keep continuity explicit: who is where, what they wear, what they hold, time of day, and how each shot relates to the one before (continuation, cut, or story transition).
- Answer with ONE JSON object only. No prose before or after it, no markdown fences, no comments.

Production direction: Cartoon (feature-animation CG).
Storytelling: Feature-animation storytelling: clear wants, big readable emotions, visual gags that pay off, a warm ensemble. Scenes are built around physical business and expressive reactions. Dialogue is short and playful; silences and looks do real work.
Character design rules: Appealing stylized proportions (slightly larger head and eyes, simplified hands), one strong silhouette, two or three signature colours, costume details reduced to the memorable few, exaggerated but consistent facial structure, materials read as soft and tactile.
Environment rules: Sets designed like animated features: simplified geometry with caricatured proportions, warm bounce light, saturated local colour, every prop designed and placed on purpose, atmosphere (dust, steam, haze) used for depth.
Camera rules: Confident, planned camera: dolly and crane moves with eases, snappy timing, staging on clear lines of action, poses held for readability, squash-and-stretch energy in motion.

Language: English. Write natural spoken English in "text"; leave "textAr" empty.

TIMELINES: each existing character's age is their age now and "bornAbout" is the year they were born. Every year in a character's own life — a marriage, a loss, work, a journey — falls after they were about 16 and not after this year. A year before a character was born appears only as history they read or heard about, never as something they or their spouse lived.

Write the script for these scenes of "The Harbour Office" (episode).
Logline: Elias and Najm confront a reluctant harbour master to uncover a hidden truth in a decades-old logbook, sparking a new lead from the static of the sky.
Synopsis: The morning after the mysterious signal, Elias and Najm visit the Kerran Point harbour office, a salt-worn outpost where the records of the 1987 storm are kept. They are met by Ingrid Dahl, the brisk and bureaucratic harbour master who views the tragedy of the Mariner as a closed chapter that should remain undisturbed.

While Elias’s frustration grows, Najm employs his librarian's patience, navigating Ingrid's rigid rules with gentle persistence. Eventually worn down, Ingrid grants them access to the sealed 1987 logbook. Inside, they discover a shocking discrepancy: the last radio entry from Ruth Moore indicates the Mariner turned back toward the point, contradicting the official inquiry's claim that the ship drifted out to sea.

Returning to the workshop in a state of quiet shock, the men wait as night falls. A new meteor shower streaks across the dark sky, and the old valve radio crackles to life once more. Through the static, a voice provides a specific bearing, pointing toward a location near the coast.

The episode closes on a poignant contrast: Elias, haunted by the sea and refusing to leave the shore, stares out the window at the horizon the bearing points to, while Najm unrolls a nautical chart to plot the coordinates.

Each scene plays for about 44 seconds, so 2–6 beats per scene; a beat is one piece of action (what we see, present tense, specific and filmable in a few seconds) followed by 0–4 short dialogue lines. Lines are short (spoken in under 6 seconds). 
If a scene already has beats, improve and complete them rather than discarding what is there.
Return JSON: { scenes: [{ sceneId, beats: [{ action, lines: [{ characterName, text, textAr?, delivery? }] }] }] }. "delivery" is a short performance note (e.g. "quietly, not looking up").

beats.action: Wide shot: The salt-worn harbour office clings to the cliff edge. A cold wind whips Elias's yellow raincoat, making it flare out like a skirt as he and Najm walk up the wooden wharf.
Mid shot: Elias walks with a slight stoop, his left hand bandaged and tucked into his pocket. He looks at the office with a mixture of dread and longing.

lines.text: It's been too long since I stepped foot in there.

beats.action: Najm walks beside him, his movements measured. He adjusts his glasses, his eyes scanning the horizon before fixing on the destination.

lines.text: The truth doesn't age, Elias. It only gathers dust.

beats.action: Close-up on the heavy wooden door of the office. The paint is peeling, and a brass knocker shaped like an anchor hangs crookedly.
Interior: Ingrid Dahl is a rigid silhouette behind the massive oak desk. She brings a mechanical date-stamper down with a thunderous THUMP on a document.
Elias and Najm enter. Elias removes his navy cap, clutching it to his chest. Ingrid looks up, her steel-blue eyes piercing and cold.

lines.text: Office hours begin at eight. It is currently eight-oh-two. State your business.

beats.action: Elias steps forward, his voice cracking slightly. He gestures with his bandaged hand toward the shelves of archival boxes.

lines.text: I need to see the 1987 logs. The Mariner's final entries.

beats.action: Ingrid doesn't move a muscle, her posture like a plumb line. She points a sharp finger toward a framed set of regulations on the wall.

lines.text: The 1987 logs were sealed by order of the official inquiry. They are not for public consumption.

beats.action: Elias begins to pace the small room, his rubber boots squeaking on the floor. He throws his arms up in a gesture of frustration.

lines.text: It was my wife! My wife was on that ship!

beats.action: Najm gently places a hand on Elias's shoulder to still him. He steps forward, leaning in toward Ingrid with a soft, scholarly smile.

lines.text: Of course, the seal is paramount. But as a fellow keeper of records, I worry... is the ink fading on that specific vellum?

beats.action: Close-up on Ingrid. Her brow furrows. The mention of 'ink fading' and 'vellum' catches her professional interest. Her rigid shoulders drop a fraction of an inch.

lines.text: The 1987 ledger is leather-bound. Standard maritime grade.

beats.action: Najm nods slowly, scratching his beard, playing the part of the concerned academic.

lines.text: Still, the humidity in these stone walls can be treacherous for gold-embossed spines.

beats.action: Ingrid lets out a long, defeated sigh. She turns and walks toward the heavy iron safe embedded in the stone wall, the silver whistle on her chest glinting.

lines.text: Five minutes. Under my direct supervision.

beats.action: Close-up: Ingrid inserts a heavy brass key. We hear the metallic CLICK-CLACK of the tumblers shifting. The sound is magnified and heavy.
The safe door swings open with a low, metallic groan, sending a small puff of archival dust into the air. Elias leans in, breathless.
Ingrid reaches into the dark interior and pulls out a thick, leather-bound book with '1987' embossed in fading gold on the cover.
Najm takes the book with trembling reverence. He lays it open on the scarred oak desk. The pages are yellowed and smell of brine.
Najm's finger slides rapidly down the columns of dates and weather reports, then stops abruptly on the final entry.
Extreme close-up: The handwritten ink is shaky. We see the words: '11:42 PM - Radio Officer Moore reports engine failure. Turning back toward the point.'
Elias's face enters the frame, his hazel eyes widening. He reads the line, his breath hitching in his chest.

lines.text: Turning back... they were coming home.

beats.action: Elias stares at the page, his bandaged left hand trembling violently. He doesn't look up at Ingrid, only at the ink.
Najm closes the book gently and slides it back toward Ingrid. He looks at her, not with triumph, but with a heavy, quiet sadness.
Elias and Najm turn and walk out of the office in a stunned, heavy silence. Their footsteps echo on the wharf.
Shot of Ingrid standing alone by her desk. She watches them leave through the window, her rigid expression softening into one of deep conflict.
Wide shot: The two small figures are silhouetted against a deep purple and orange sky. They walk slowly back toward the village, the sea crashing against the cliffs below.
Tracking shot: The wind has died down. Elias's yellow raincoat is still, his shoulders slumped. Najm walks in step with him, a silent companion.
They reach the wooden door of Elias's workshop. The first few stars are beginning to blink awake in the twilight.

lines.text: Tonight is the peak of the shower.

beats.action: Interior: The workshop is dim, lit only by the green-shaded lamp. Elias sits on a stool, his eyes locked on the dial of the valve radio.
Najm stands by the window, meticulously cleaning his glasses with a soft cloth. He looks up at the black void of the sky.
Close-up on the radio dial. The needle is perfectly still. The silence of the room is heavy.
Suddenly, a single, brilliant streak of a meteor flashes across the window glass, casting a momentary white light over the room.
Wide shot through the workshop window: The sky suddenly erupts. Dozens of meteors streak downward in a flurry of white and gold light.
The valve radio begins to hum. Inside the chassis, the glass valves start to glow a warm, pulsing orange, mirroring the stars outside.
Elias leans in, his face bathed in the orange glow. The hum grows into a vibration that rattles the glass jar of screws on the workbench.
The radio erupts in a scream of static. Elias frantically turns the tuning knob, his bandaged hand gripping the plastic dial.
The static snaps clear. A feminine voice—soft, distorted, but unmistakably Ruth's—cuts through the noise.
Najm quickly grabs a pencil, scribbling the numbers onto a scrap of paper as Elias freezes, a tear tracking through the lines of his weathered cheek.
The last meteor fades from the sky. The orange glow in the valves vanishes instantly, and the radio collapses back into a hollow hiss of static.
Elias stands up and walks to the window. He stares out at the black horizon in the direction of the bearing, his reflection ghost-like in the glass.

lines.text: I can't go back out there, Najm. I can't.

beats.action: Cut to the workbench. Najm ignores the sadness and focuses on the task. He unrolls a large, weathered nautical chart with a sharp snap.
Close-up: Najm places the pencil on the chart, carefully plotting the bearing from Kerran Point. He circles a specific coordinate near the coast with a determined look.

lines.text: Then I will go for both of us.
